predecessors.note: The ulus lies inside Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row (1206-1293) throughout.

capitals.name: Sarai
capitals.note: Infobox capital Sarai (western wing, later the whole state), Sighnaq (eastern wing); 'Batu settled in the lower Volga after 1242 and never returned to Mongolia'. The page gives no founding date for Sarai; before 1242 no seat is named (Jochi's lands lay on the Irtysh).

rulers.name: Jochi
rulers.note: Golden Horde infobox 'c. 1225 (first): Jochi'; text 'Jochi (d. 1225) was given the lands (an ulus) around the Irtysh River'; the Jochi page: died c.1225, news of it reaching Genghis in 1225 or 1227, so the interval to Batu's 1227 is bridged.

rulers.name: Batu
rulers.note: Reign 1227-1255 (Batu page); Jochi's death is given as c.1225 (Jochi page, news in 1225 or 1227).

rulers.name: Sartaq
rulers.note: 'After Batu died in 1256, his son Sartaq Khan was appointed by Möngke Khan' (the infobox gives Batu's reign to 1255). The page dates neither accession nor death; the years are bridged.

rulers.name: Ulaghchi
rulers.note: 'The infant Ulaghchi succeeded him under the regency of Boragchin Khatun, Batu's widow'; no years on the page; bridged up to Berke's enthronement in 1257 or 1258.

rulers.name: Berke
rulers.note: Enthroned 1257 or 1258; died in 1265 on the way to a crossing near Tiflis (Berke-Hulagu page; the Golden Horde page and others say 1266). Sartaq (1255-56) is not listed.

rulers.name: Mengu-Timur (Möngke Temür)
rulers.note: Nominated by Kublai; reigned 1266-1280. Töde Möngke follows (below).

rulers.name: Töde Möngke
rulers.note: 'Mengu-Timur was succeeded in 1281 by his brother Töde Möngke' (Golden Horde page); the Mengu-Timur page ends that reign in 1280, so the start is taken as 1280 to leave no gap. Talabuga took over in 1287 (Talabuga page).

rulers.name: Talabuga
rulers.note: Infobox 'Reign: 1287-1291'; 'In 1287, Talabuga became the Khan of the Ulus of Jochi'; slew Töde Möngke; ambushed and assassinated by Nogai's forces and replaced with Toqta in 1291.

rulers.name: Toqta
rulers.note: Replaced Talabuga in 1291 after Nogai's forces killed him; the reign continues past 1293 in the golden-horde dossier.

region.text: the lands around the Irtysh (its south-western Siberian reach) and the steppe of Orda and Batu

ledger.note: c.1225: the ulus of Jochi stands on the Irtysh. Golden Horde infobox 'c. 1225'; 'Jochi (d. 1225) received lands around the Irtysh River'; the Jochi page: death 'c. 1225', news of it came 'in either 1225 or 1227', 'Batu was confirmed as ruler of his father's territories'. The Batu page gives Batu's reign as 1227-1255. [fx-36 H08, 1 Nov 2026: the Irtysh reading is narrowed from the whole 300 km buffer of the river (6,511 cells; 4,747 outside the Kazakh Steppe, among them Khanty-Mansiy 1,029, Xinjiang 786, western Mongolia 592, Tomsk 174) to its south-western Siberian reach (Tyumen, Omsk, Novosibirsk, Altai Krai, Kurgan: 1,769 cells outside the Kazakh Steppe), and the same reach is kept in every later keyframe, so the 1236 snap (4,631 cells removed) and the 1267 one no longer drop it. Golden Horde page: 'Jochi (d. 1225) was given the lands (an ulus) around the Irtysh River.' White Horde page: Orda's ulus formed around 1225 and 'included western Central Asia and south-western Siberia'; Golden Horde page: its territory at its peak 'extended from Siberia and Central Asia'. No page puts Xinjiang, Khanty-Mansiy or western Mongolia in the ulus, and none records a loss of south-western Siberia after 1225, so it stays Jochid to 1293 (confidence 1 for the extent).]

1225 (bridging a silence): Khwarazm and the Otrar oasis are Jochid land from the ulus's start. No page dates the assignment: the Jochi page says Genghis 'intended' the Syr Darya towns and Gurganj Jochi conquered in 1219-20 'to become part of Jochi's territories' and is silent on the ulus; the Siege of Gurganj page is silent on who received Urgench; the Khwarazm page says only that 'The region of Khwarazm was split between the White Horde and Jagatai Khanate' (undated); the Golden Horde page speaks of 'the Golden Horde's lands in Khorazm' that Alghu 'smashed' and of Alghu 'seizing Otrar and Khorazm'. The first dated trace is therefore Alghu's seizure c.1263 (/ledger loss). Added at the reviewer's request so that the land Alghu seizes was Jochid before; the southern part of Khwarazm (Kath, Khiva) may always have been Chagatai's (Sufi dynasty page: 'allocated to the Chagatai khans').

region.text: the Kazakh steppe, the Aral steppe and the Urals that the Kimek-Kipchak row held to 1226

ledger.note: 1227: the steppe of the Kimek-Kipchak row passes to the ulus. Kimek page: 'The Mongols conquered the remnant of the Kimak Khanate, and its lands were assigned to the Ulus of Jochi' (13th century, undated). The year is Cliopatria's step in the kimek-kipchak-confederation dossier (ledger loss 1227, the same cells; the 1227 Mongol Empire shape holds them): the Golden Horde page has Jochi's ulus 'around the Irtysh River', says 'Jochi died before he could significantly expand it' and has the kurultai of 1229 decide 'to subdue the Kipchaks', so the page does not date the handover and a later year is as likely. Added in fx-04: the Kimek loss had pointed at mongol-empire, so the 1236 keyframe had to pull these cells over in one jump (snap).
1236: Batu takes Volga Bulgaria. The army 'crossed the Volga and invaded Volga Bulgaria in 1236'; the Golden Horde page: 'Volga Bulgaria falls' in 1236.

region.text: the Alan lands from the Kuban headwaters to the Darial Gorge

ledger.note: 1240: Maghas falls and the Alan country is lost. 'In 1239/1240 the Mongols invaded, stormed and destroyed the capital, Maghas'; the siege 'began in November or December 1239 and lasted until February 1240'. The page does not name the Jochid ulus; the Alan lands from the Kuban headwaters to the Darial Gorge lie in Batu's sphere (the Golden Horde page has Mengu-Timur against the Alans in 1277-78).

region.text: the Pontic-Caspian steppe of the Cumans

ledger.note: 1241: the Cuman steppe becomes Jochid. 'the final blow came in 1241, when the Cuman confederacy ceased to exist as a political entity'; the remaining tribes became subjects of the Mongols 'as part of what was to be known as the Golden Horde'.

region.text: the Volga-Don steppe west of the Urals that remained

ledger.note: 1241: the last Kimek-Kipchak steppe becomes Jochid. Cumans page: 'The final blow came in 1241, when Cuman control over the Pontic steppes ended' and the confederation 'ceased to exist as a political entity', its people 'becoming subjects and mixing with their Mongol conquerors' 'as part of what was to be known as the Golden Horde'; the Kimek page: its lands 'were assigned to the Ulus of Jochi'. Mirror of the kimek-kipchak-confederation loss of 1241, added in fx-04 (it had pointed at mongol-empire, so the 1241 keyframe took these cells in one jump).
1242: Batu settles on the lower Volga. 'Batu settled in the lower Volga after 1242 and never returned to Mongolia'; the capital is Sarai (the page does not date its founding).

region.text: the grand principality of Vladimir, the Rostov-Suzdal land

ledger.note: 1243: Yaroslav II of Vladimir acknowledges Batu. 'In 1243, he was summoned by Batu Khan to his capital Sarai' and 'returned to Vladimir with honours' (Yaroslav II page); the Golden Horde page has all the senior princes of Rus', Yaroslav II among them, acknowledging Batu's supremacy; the Batu Khan page has Batu confirming Yaroslav as suzerain over the other Rus' princes. The earlier date 1252 (Batu 'installed Alexander as grand prince of Vladimir in 1252') was a later act, not the start of the vassalage (reviewer, 2026-10-19). The counterpart row principality-of-rostov-suzdal ends in 1240 and shares Wikidata Q83546 with principality-of-vladimir-suzdal (from 1294): if eu-16 writes one dossier it takes the earlier slug, which is used here.

1245: Daniel of Galicia submits. 'Daniel pledged allegiance in 1245' (the Batu page has him summoned to Sarai and submitting, undated); the Rus' princes had acknowledged Batu's supremacy in the 1240s. The mongol-empire dossier records the Mongol conquest of the Rus' principalities 1237-1240.

region.text: the Caucasus: the Derbend pass, the Terek and Shabran

ledger.note: 1262: the Berke–Hulagu war opens in the Caucasus. 'Clashes with Berke began in 1262. Hulagu marched north through the Derbend pass and was ambushed on the Terek by Nogai's army'; Nogai had been raiding the Caucasus after Ain Jalut (1260).

c.1263: Alghu takes Otrar and Khwarazm. 'Alghu seized Otrar and Khorazm' (undated in the page; Alghu reigned 1260-1265 and fought Kaidu and the Jochids near Otrar in 1263 per the Alghu page): a bridging date. Region (repair): Otrar (200 km) and the Khwarezm region, the same as the ulus-of-chagatai gain; the 400 km Gurganj circle was replaced because it covers 436,000 km2 and cuts the Aral steppe.

1265: the war dies with its principals. Hulagu died on 8 February 1265; 'Berke marched toward a crossing near Tiflis but died on the way' (1265 on the war page, 1266 elsewhere). No peace is dated and no frontier change is given; the Terek ice battle of 1262 was Berke's victory.

c.1267: the Jochids are back in Khwarazm. The page says only 'A 1267 peace gave one-third of Transoxiana to Kaidu and Mengu-Timur'; the recovery of Otrar and Khwarazm from Alghu's heirs is not dated. Cliopatria's 1294 shape carries the land, so a bridging date is used. Region (repair): as /ledger loss 1263; mirror of the ulus-of-chagatai loss.

c.1280: Bulgaria becomes a Horde vassal. 'In 1280 he had Ivaylo executed at a feast'; Nogai 'made George Terter I a vassal, then placed his associate Smilets on the Bulgarian throne. Bulgaria remained a Horde vassal'. The year is the page's date for Ivaylo's death; the vassalage itself is undated. Repair 2026-10-19: the Second Bulgarian Empire page, opened again, gives no year for the vassalage either ('George I Terter ... bringing even stronger Mongol influence' after 1280; 'In 1300 ... an end to Mongol interference'), so the confidence is lowered to 1.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; the vassalage of Galicia-Volhynia, Vladimir and Bulgaria goes on in the golden-horde dossier, which restarts the tribute events in 1294.
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; the grand principality of Vladimir stays a Horde vassal in the golden-horde dossier (1294).
1293: bookkeeping end of the ulus; Bulgaria remains a Horde vassal under Smilets (Nogai page).

1293: the Jochid ulus carries on as the Golden Horde. A bookkeeping break, not a historical one: the Golden Horde infobox gives 'c. 1225' to 1502 as one state, while Cliopatria's Golden Horde row begins in 1294 (the golden-horde dossier says the same).

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Volga Bulgaria and the Cuman steppe
wars.outcome: Batu crossed the Volga in 1236, took Volga Bulgaria and ended the Cuman confederacy in 1241; the Rus' principalities were then made tributaries and Batu camped on the Volga in 1242.
wars.note: The Rus' campaign (December 1237 Ryazan to December 1240 Kiev) and the 1241 raid on Hungary are in the mongol-empire dossier; no land beyond the steppe was kept west of the Carpathians.

wars.name: Berke–Hulagu war

zones.text: the Caucasus, fought over from the Derbend pass to Shabran

wars.outcome: Hulagu was routed on the ice of the Terek in 1262 and fell back into Azerbaijan; Hulagu and Berke both died in 1265. The page gives no territorial result and no peace.
wars.note: Berke allied with the Mamluks against Hulagu; Nogai commanded his armies.

wars.name: Nogai’s Balkan and Central European campaigns
wars.outcome: Raids on the Byzantine Empire (1265, 1271, 1274, 1282), a siege of Ivaylo at Silistra (1278-79), his execution in 1280 and the vassalage of Bulgaria; Hungary (1285) and Poland (1287-88) were invaded and the raids failed.

certainty.note: Steppe frontiers throughout; the Caucasus frontier with the Ilkhanate is only a zone of campaigns (1262-65), not a line.

notes:
The Jochid ulus before Cliopatria's Golden Horde row (1294): the golden-horde dossier says its pre-1294 years are not drawn separately and that an ulus dossier would need it to start earlier; this dossier is that ulus. No Cliopatria shape exists, so all keyframes are new, and the last (1267-1293) simply reuses the Golden Horde 1294 shape because the pages date no Jochid border change after the 1267 peace. The ulus lies inside Cliopatria's Mongol Empire row throughout; the rendering agents should draw it over that row.

The mongol-empire dossier records the 1237-1240 conquest of the Rus' principalities as vassal events of the Mongol Empire. The two vassal events here (Galicia-Volhynia 1245, Vladimir 1252) are the dates at which the Jochid pages show Batu as the suzerain; the orchestrator should decide whether the mongol-empire events are re-pointed to this dossier for the colour of the tint. Kiev, Chernigov and Pereyaslavl are not repeated.

Dates that disagree: Jochi's death c.1225 (infobox) or 1227 (Batu's accession); Berke's death 1265 (Berke-Hulagu page) or 1266 (Nogai and other pages); Mengu-Timur's independence from Kublai is not dated by the Golden Horde page (it mentions neither Talas nor 1269). The 1267 peace gave one third of Transoxiana to Kaidu and Mengu-Timur; the pages do not say where Mengu-Timur's part lay and Kaidu's pages give Bukhara to Kaidu, so no Transoxiana land is drawn as Jochid.
